title: Users, groups and sudo
summary: Who you are on the machine, what root is, and what sudo really does.

text: Every user has a number (uid) and belongs to groups. (id prints all this on one line.)
- Groups share rights: every member of devs gets the group's rights on files that belong to devs.
root is the administrator: no permission check stops it.
- Services get their own users, so a broken web server can't touch your files.

scheme: apt install jq   runs as root, for this command
text: sudo runs one command as root, if you're allowed to (the sudo group, or wheel on Red Hat).
- Use it only for the command that needs it, never out of habit.
- sudo remembers your password for a few minutes, then asks again.
